title: Cloud retail tile governance and asset quickcheck
content:
Purpose
---
This is a lightweight, practical quickcheck for cloud marketplace tile (aka product card) submissions for our retail/vertical partners and co-sell partners that require a slightly different onboarding flow. The doc combines copy variants for marketing tiles, a minimum-viable technical acceptance checklist, and a short smoke-test runbook so partners and internal PM/ops can get a tile live without multiple back-and-forths.

Scope and audience
- Primary: partner onboarding managers, partner solutions engineers, GTM ops
- Secondary: legal intake, security review, billing/product ops
- Not in scope: deep legal contract negotiation, custom integration engineering (those have separate playbooks)

Top-level acceptance gates (stoplight)
1) Branding & copy: tile title + 2 variants of description, confirm trademark/licensing.
2) Technical compatibility: entitlement API, trial provisioning, SSO (if required).
3) Billing & SKU mapping: marketplace SKU + redemption flow validated in staging.
4) Security & data residency: data handling doc attached, PII flagging, required DSR obligations noted.
5) Telemetry & observability: event taxonomy defined and test pings implemented.

Minimum-viable technical checklist (quick, try to keep to 90 minutes of work for SRE/solutions):
- Marketplace sandbox account: partner assigned, credentials validated.
- SKU exists in billing catalog and maps to internal product_id. (Billing owner: @Diego)
- Trial provisioning endpoint: POST /marketplace/trials responds 200 in staging and creates internal trial_id.
- Entitlement callback: marketplace sends callback -> our /entitlement/handler accepts and sets state to active.
- Usage metering: sample meter event ingested in staging (meter name: tokenized_calls); verify ingestion within 10m.
- Redirects/tiles: tile landing link resolves to documented integration page, no 3xx loops.
- SSO (optional): SAML metadata uploaded and assertion validated with a sample user.
- Logs: 3 sample events/requests captured with correlation id.
- Security checklist: partner security questionnaire submitted or waived. If PII: KMS key policy reviewed.

Copy variants (tile title and short descriptions) — keep short, A/B testable. Aim for 1 line title, 1–2 sentence description, one CTA.
- Title (A): "Low-latency LLM inference for Retail Agents"
  Description (A): "Serve personalized shopping assistants with predictable latency and cost — Redwood-managed inference with regional isolation and SLA-backed throughput."
  CTA: "Get started (free trial)"

- Title (B): "Server-grade LLM APIs for retail CX"
  Description (B): "Integrate high-throughput LLM inference into recommendations, chat, and search workflows. Dedicated capacity options and automatic fallbacks keep experiences live."
  CTA: "Claim trial credits"

- Short elevator blurb (for tile hover): "Enterprise-grade LLM serving with predictable costs, privacy controls, and built-in fault tolerance."

Differentiation bullets (1–3 lines max) to include as feature list on tile expanded view:
- Dedicated GPU pools and auto-bursting for holiday peaks
- Prefix caching and batching tuned for short conversational flows
- Region-aware routing & private deployment options for regulated stores
- Telemetry at token-level for cost and latency attribution

Trial and entitlement scenarios (matrix)
- Free credits (self-serve): immediate provisioning, 14-day usage cap, no payment method.
- Marketplace trial (partner-managed): token voucher issued by marketplace; our entitlement callback must mark trial as active and map voucher -> internal trial_id.
- Managed pilot (enterprise): dedicated provision, requires contract + SSO + KMS integration before tile goes live.

Smoke test runbook (10–15 minutes to validate a staging tile)
1) Open tile in staging marketplace and click CTA -> should redirect to /partner/landing?tile=partnerX
2) Submit a trial request (self-serve) and confirm a trial email + trial_id in admin console.
3) Simulate marketplace entitlement callback with sample webhook (payload in Confluence link above). Verify internal state transitions: pending -> active -> expired.
4) Send 5 sample inference requests using test API key and confirm responses and token-level metrics in telemetry dashboard.
5) Validate billing event emitted with meter=tokenized_calls and amount>0.
6) If SSO expected: run SAML assertion test user.
7) Capture screenshots and attach to ticket for launch readiness.

Risk and failure modes (fast triage pointers)
- Entitlement callback 500s: check endpoint health, retry logic, and marketplace logs. If persistent, fallback to manual voucher redemption flow and escalate to partner-ops.
- Billing mismatch: confirm SKU mapping and timezone of metering. If mismatch, pause tile and run postmortem.
- Elevated latency on peak: check autoscaling policy and GPU allocation; consider rolling out reduced-burst config while investigating.

Operational notes (internal)
- Suggested default autoscale: min 2 workers per cluster, burst to 8 during peak windows for retail tiles.
- Prefix caching TTL: 30s for chat agents with short context.
- Recommended quantization profile: int8 for cost-sensitive trials; list profile id in asset repo PR.

Launch checklist (preflight)
- [ ] Copy approved by partner marketing and Redwood brand team
- [ ] SKU mapped and billing owner assigned
- [ ] Entitlement webhook validated in staging
- [ ] Security questionnaire completed or documented exception
- [ ] Telemetry pings and event schema published
- [ ] Support runbook created and linked in Jira ticket
- [ ] Legal sign-off for partner co-marketing (if co-sell)

Partner-facing email snippet (short)
Subject: Your marketplace tile is ready for validation
Hi <PartnerName>,
Quick update — staging tile is up. Please confirm copy and perform the 10-min smoke test (steps attached). If everything looks good we can schedule a go-live window this Thursday.
Thanks — Maya (GTMP)

Notes to self / open questions
- Do we want to auto-enable billing alerts for new retail tiles (suggested yes)?
- Who is the on-call rotation owner for marketplace entitlement incidents? (Tentative: Diego week-of-launch)
- Decide if promotional credits should be visible in console or only via tile CTA.

Attachments and artifacts
- Link to sample payloads: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/GTMP/marketplace-callback-examples
- Asset repo PR for tile images: https://github.com/redwood-inference/marketplace-assets/pull/87
- Billing mapping doc: JIRA-2148

Quick acceptance heuristic (for PMs)
If all minimum-viable checklist items are green and the partner approves copy, mark tile Ready-for-Publish and book a 30m release window with platform-ops.

-- end of quickcheck --

(Working draft - will convert to canonical checklist and add to GTM playbooks folder once first partner launch completes.)
